Figure 2:Null events break memory, and only through memory.(a) Three null events in one SwingXtimes episode (front camera; first event of three separate rollouts): the robot pauses, rolls its wrist, or grasps the air above the cube and returns, and no object moves.
Memory keeps 32 frames sampled uniformly over the episode, each stamped with its time step. In the visible condition the frames of the event enter memory and the stamps advance over it, whereas in the hidden condition neither happens.
(b) Successes over 50 paired episodes of the released FrameSamp-Modul policy; dashed line: no event. Air-grasps are not used on PickXtimes, where the returning gripper often re-closes around the cube.

header: 5Why: A Memory Filled by Time Counts Null Events

images.caption:
Figure 6:Removing the clock is not enough.(a)NoClock, trained without time encoding, ignores rescaled time stamps, yet two 5-second pauses still break it; hiding them restores both models (PickXtimes, successes of 50 paired episodes; both tasks inAppendixF).
(b) A pause enters a time-sampled memory by two routes: time stamps keep advancing over unchanged frames, which onlyClockreceives, and pause frames take a share of the 32 slots, which both models receive (10 slots in the episode shown, about 450 working steps; frames from its first pause).
(c) Without any pause, blocks of null slots alone degradeNoClock(Sec.F.6). The dashed line marks the share two 5-second pauses take.

Figure 9:A fidget and an air-grasp, frame by frame(SwingXtimes episode 18, released FrameSamp-Modul, visible condition; front and wrist cameras, unedited frames).
Both events start after policy step 48, before the robot has picked up the cube, and the policy is not queried while they run.
The fidget rolls the wrist back and forth around its held target, which the wrist camera shows as a rotating scene; the air-grasp lowers the gripper to the cube, closes it on air, and returns to the starting pose.
Neither moves the cube (0.00 cm in the evaluator’s log), and both end where they started, yet every frame enters memory.
The two rows come from separate rollouts of the same episode; a pause, which leaves the image still, is shown inFig.2.
